meta_title: Sapphire Creators – Marketing, web design and AI efficiency
meta_desc: Sapphire Creators is a team of developers. On the outside we build marketing, websites and films people remember. On the inside, AI tools that take routine work off your team.
hero_sub: We're a team of developers. For your customers we build marketing and websites people remember. For your team we build AI tools that do the routine work – from the quote email to the wiring diagram.
manifest_text: Most companies either polish what people see – or improve what happens behind it. But a sapphire only sparkles when both sides are right. So we build marketing that gets seen, and AI that gives your team hours back. No templates. Just code.
stat1_text: Every project starts from zero – with an idea that only exists once.
stat2_text: No site builders, no off-the-shelf plugins, no limits.
stat3_text: Marketing, film, web and AI automation – all from one team.
s1_text: Walk-through showrooms and product worlds right in the browser. No app, no download – open a link and dive in.
s2_text: Launch and product films that are rendered, not shot: with real 3D models, original music and voice.
s3_text: Websites that tell a story as you scroll. Just like this one.
s4_text: Copy, images and voices in every language – generated, curated and tuned precisely to your brand.
s5_text: Invitation films, event pages and countdowns that don't just inform people but bring them on site.
s6_text: One source, many countries: websites that build themselves for every language and every market.
s7_title: And everything that doesn't have a name yet.
zoom_inner:

team_title: A team of developers. Not ad people.
team_text: There are no account managers between you and the people who build your project. You talk directly to developers who are equally at home in design, 3D, film, code and AI – whether it's about your website or the processes behind it.
r1_text: Interfaces and websites that feel different from anything you know.
r2_text: We model, animate and render products – sometimes before they even exist.
r3_text: Editing, sound design, music and voice. Frame by frame, note by note.
r4_text: Tools that do the routine work: drawings, quotes, reports, translations – checked and traceable.
process_title: From rough stone to the first wow.
p1_text: We dive into your product, your customers and your processes – until we know where attention is missing and where time gets lost.
p2_text: Instead of slides you get something that runs, early on: a page to scroll through or a tool that works with your real data.
p3_text: Design, code, 3D, film and AI are made in the same team. Every result gets checked – automatically and by people.
p4_text: We take it live or into your daily work, measure what works and keep building. Good marketing and good processes are never finished.
contact_text: Tell us about your product, your event – or the task that costs your team hours every week.
footer_tagline: Built by developers – without a single template.
why_title: Hard on ourselves. Clear in the cut.
why_text: After diamond, sapphire is one of the hardest materials in nature. What makes it sparkle is the cut – and a brilliant has two sides that both have to be right.
work_meta: Massage studio, Tamm · Website & scroll story
work_text: A site that feels like the treatment itself: warm light, calm – and a moment to breathe in the middle of the scroll.
pj_meta_desc: Selected work by Sapphire Creators: the scroll story for Melanie’s Massage and Project Stack – the complete control engineering of a machine, built with AI.
pj_sub: This is what we have built – outside and inside. Websites that are online right now, and AI projects that work inside companies. Some of them we can only show anonymously.
c1_lead: What does a massage feel like before you even enter the room? We turned a small studio's website into a scroll story: warm evening light, calm – and a moment to breathe in the middle of the page.
c1_video_caption: A real recording of the live site, scrolled once from top to bottom.
c1_s1: The old site did its job – but looked like many others. Fonts and icons came from third-party servers, and a single photo weighed more than 2 MB.
c1_s2: The site should feel like the treatment: slow, warm, quiet. The entire colour palette comes from the photo of the treatment room – evening light, wood, linen.
c1_s3: An arch that opens into the whole room as you scroll. Treatments that glide past sideways. A breathing pause where the page goes dark. And prices you understand at a glance.
cs1_text: Down from 2,745 KB. The page is there before you get impatient – even on the go.
cs2_text: No Google Fonts, no external scripts. Good for speed and for privacy.
cs3_text: German and English, one click to switch.
cs4_text: From phone and iPad to the big monitor.

fc1_text: Light enters the stone through the crown – and so does the first look at your company. Websites, films, 3D worlds and campaigns: everything people experience when they meet you for the first time.
fc2_text: Below the setting lies the part nobody sees. It sends the light back – cut it badly and the whole stone goes dull. In your company that's quotes, drawings, documentation and data. That's where our AI goes to work.
fc3_text: Marketing without working processes promises what everyday life can't keep. Efficiency without visibility goes unnoticed. We cut both sides – in one team.

work2_text: A pneumatic pallet stacker needed its complete control engineering. From a 3D model and a sequence description, AI produced the drawings, the control cabinet and the PLC program – tested in a simulation before a human signed them off.
dwg_alt: Illustration of a control drawing: a pneumatic cylinder with a 5/2-way valve and three current paths with relay, valve coil and indicator lamp
c2s_lead: A machine builder had developed a pneumatic pallet stacker. What was missing was the complete control engineering: pneumatic diagram, wiring diagram, control cabinet and PLC program. We built it with AI – and had everything checked automatically before a human signed it off.
c2s_status: Handed over to the engineering department
conf_long: Why anonymous? The project is confidential. So we show no original drawings, no names and no part numbers – only how we worked. The drawings are illustrations; every number comes from the real project.
conf_short: Confidential client project, anonymised. All numbers are real, the drawings are illustrations.
c2s_caption: An illustration in the style of the real drawings – the originals stay with the client.
io_o4: Control cabinet layout · 3 sheets · with heat balance
sot_text: Everything comes from a single data model: devices, inputs and outputs, terminals, cables and messages. The drawings, lists and program are generated from it. Change one sensor and every document changes with it – and the checks run again from the start.
tl1: 3D model, sequence description, drawing, video – and one sentence: “I need a pneumatic diagram, a wiring diagram, the control cabinet and a PLC program.”
tl2: All drawings, lists and the PLC program. Plus a simulation in which the program is already running the machine.
tl3: “Some symbols aren't shown correctly.” Every symbol is redrawn against the standards and the manufacturers' documents.
tl4: “There must be no errors anywhere.” Our own checking programs now read every line, every terminal, every address.
tl5: Six documents, revision 02 – ready for the engineering department.
tw_text: We didn't just write the PLC program – we ran it: against a model of the machine, one cycle every 10 milliseconds. Every movement that would be mechanically impossible or dangerous counts as a failure – including an emergency stop in every single step.
tw1: Store and retrieve at full capacity
tw2: Emergency stop in every step: storing
tw3: Emergency stop in every step: retrieving
tw10: Pallet left on the lifting frame
tw13: Cycle time measured in the model
au_title: Checking until there's nothing left to find.
au_text: For the second round we wrote checking programs that read every drawing by machine: overlaps, missing junction dots, terminals, cable cores, addresses. In the end there were zeros everywhere.
au2: Cross-references pointing to the wrong column
au3: Terminals – identical in drawing and list
au4: Every I/O address matches between wiring diagram and program
op_text: An AI that pretends to know everything is dangerous. So every assumption is marked visibly in the drawings – and goes back to the people who are responsible for it. Seven open points, clearly named:
op4: Cylinder switches – not in the 3D model
op6: Operator panel and second emergency stop
ss1_text: From the request at 8:12 pm to the complete package at 9:36 pm.
ss2_text: Pneumatics, wiring and control cabinet – to ISO 1219, IEC 60617 and EN 60204-1.
ss3_text: Passed – including an emergency stop in every step.
ss4_text: In the final automated review across all 27 sheets.

aic_text: A machine builder needed the complete control engineering for a new pallet stacker. The request came in the evening, 84 minutes later the first complete draft was there – and the next morning the checked package went to the engineering department.
pr1: AI delivers drafts, experts sign off. Whatever is uncertain gets marked – not hidden.
pr2: Every result is checked automatically: against rules, standards, simulations. You see what was checked – and what wasn't.
pr3: Data is maintained once. Documents, lists and code are generated from it – change something, and everything changes with it.
pr4: Before we build anything, we agree together which data each system may see. What's confidential stays confidential.
st_title: From the first conversation to a tool in daily use.
st1: You tell us where things get stuck. We listen and ask questions – no slides.
st2: We look at your processes and tell you honestly where AI helps – and where it doesn't.
st3: Something that runs, early: a tool that works with your real data.
st4: We build it into your daily work, explain it to the team and keep developing it.
faq1_a: No – and that isn't the goal either. We take routine off your team so there's more time for customers, development and decisions. Responsibility and sign-off stay with you.
faq2_a: Before we build anything, we agree together which data may be processed and where. We treat confidential projects confidentially – that's exactly why our case study is anonymised.
faq3_a: A chat window is a start. We build tools that fit your processes: with your templates, standards and data – and with built-in checks so the results hold up.
faq4_q: Do we need our own AI experts?
faq4_a: No. We build the tools so your team can use them every day, and we show how they work.
faq5_q: Is it worth it for small companies too?
faq5_a: Especially there. Where a few people carry many tasks, every hour saved makes a difference. The calculator above gives you a first impression.
faq6_a: With a conversation about your processes. Afterwards both sides know where AI really helps – and where it doesn't.
ai_cta_title: Which task should your team never again do by hand?
ai_cta_text: Tell us about it. We'll tell you honestly whether and how AI can help.
